text.p: Liberia, Africa's oldest independent republic, holds elections on Saturday to end seven years of civil war. Following are key facts about the West African country.
* Freed American slaves proclaimed the republic in 1847 with a constitution based on that of the United States.
* The name comes from the latin "liber" meaning "free".
* The capital Monrovia, named after U.S. President James Monroe, is reputedly Africa's wettest.
* The civil war launched by warlord Charles Taylor in 1989 has killed well over 150,000 people. Taylor is favourite to win the presidential and general elections.
* The United States twice evacuated its own and other foreign nationals during the war -- in 1990 and in 1996.
* Iron ore, rubber, timber and diamonds were main exports.
* It built a lucrative business offering world shipping owners flags of convenience.
* Liberia once boasted the world's largest rubber plantation -- Firestone.
* Descendants of the slaves, known as Congos, dominated political power for most of Liberia's life. Their True Whig Party enjoyed 109 years of unbroken rule until 1980.
* Masonic brotherhoods once enjoyed considerable influence.
* Master Sergeant Samuel Doe, an ethnic Krahn, one of the indigenous tribes, ended Congo rule in 1980 killing President William Tolbert and executing his ministers in public on a palm-fringed beach.
* Neighbours -- Ivory Coast (east) Guinea (north) Sierra Leone (west). Liberia fronts the Atlantic Ocean.
